text:
Registered residential sales reached 14,433 units valued at AED 42.64bn in the last four weeks, representing a 41.6% increase in volume and a 54.1% rise in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 5,985, which are recorded separately from sales transactions. The off-plan segment accounted for 57.7% of all sales, slightly down from 59.4% in the previous four weeks.

The median residential price per square foot rose to AED 1,689, marking a 1.4% increase from the previous four-week median of AED 1,665. Top selling areas by volume over the last 12 weeks include Dubai South with 3,100 sales and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,513 sales. Dubai Creek Harbour recorded the highest median price at AED 2,539 per square foot among the top volume areas, while Majan showed the lowest at AED 1,415 per square foot.

Rental activity remained robust with 110,329 Ejari contracts registered, of which 51.6% were renewals. The median annual residential rent stood at AED 68,729. Estimated gross yields for flats were highest in Zaabeel First at 8.8% and International City Phase 1 at 8.6%. Town Square followed at 7.0%, while Dubai Sports City and Dubai Production City recorded yields of 6.7% and 6.5% respectively.

Price momentum varied significantly across communities. Al Yufrah 1 showed the strongest 12-week price increase at 41.5%, followed by Dubai Industrial City at 9.4%. Conversely, Jumeirah Lakes Towers experienced the sharpest decline at 18.8%, with Palm Jumeirah down 16.7% and Al Hebiah First down 15.0%. The anomaly monitor flagged 979 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35% away from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
